input:
“A runner can never reach the end of a racecourse”, is it true? Suppose the runner travels at the constant speed and suppose it takes him T minutes to cover the first half of the course. The next quarter of the course will take T/2 minutes, the next eight will takeT/4 minutes, and, in general the portion  from 1/2^n to ½^n+1 will take T/2^n minutes. The sum of all these time intervals may be indicated symbolically by writing the following expression:

         T+T/2+T/4+…….+T/2^n +……..
This it clearly an infinite serie, but our physical experience tells us that a runner who travels at a constant speed should reach his goal in twice the time it takes for him to reach the halfway point.

2=1 Can you find what is wrong with this "proof?"? a = b (given)
a^2 = a*b (multiply both sides by a)
a^2-b^2 = a*b-b^2 (subtract -b^2 from both sides)
(a+b)(a-b) = b(a-b) (factor both sides)
(a+b) = b (divide both sides by a-b)
a+a = a (because a=b)
2a = a
2 = 1

 I don't believe failure to be "in pursuance of the original constitution" can render an amendment unconstitutional.

Amendments serve to permit the constitution to be modified - not just the wording, but the spirit. That's why there's such a large consensus required to ratify an amendment - there is no provision to restrict what an amendment can do.

This is perfectly intentional - the good judgement of the citizens of the United States should make it hard to pass an amendment, and the constitutional authors didn't believe their own judgment to be superior, for all time, than the judgment of the people living in that time.

So, to answer your question fully, not being in pursuance of the original constitution is in no way a detriment for an amendment - in fact, any amendment that's solely in pursuance of the original constitution is probably unneccessary.

Edit:
In light of your revision, Asker, I belive that you disagree with all major constitutional scholars on the meaning of "in Pursuance thereof." I haven't encountered a view elsewhere that claims the Constitution as written was intended to be impossible to change, even in spirit. On the contrary, one of the often-referenced strengths of the document is that it makes radical change possible - even to itself - without reqiring that the govenment be overthrown by force.

While I can see where your interpretation comes from, I believe you've made an error, elevating the original state of the constitution above the process it provides for its own amendment.

input: What are the different markets in economics?
label: Business & Finance
model_output:
Economics is a branch of Social Sciences that deals with the production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services. Markets in economics refer to the mechanisms through which these transactions occur, and they can be classified based on various properties such as competition level, the nature of goods, or geographic scope. The common types of markets include:

- Perfect Competition: A market structure characterized by many buyers and sellers, identical products, and free entry and exit.
- Monopolistic Competition: Many sellers offering differentiated products.
- Oligopoly: A few large firms dominate the market, and their decisions are interdependent.
- Monopoly: A single seller controls the entire market for a good or service.
- Consumer Markets: Markets where consumers buy goods and services.
- Producer Markets: Markets where goods and services are bought by producers for production purposes.
- labor markets: Where workers supply their labor and firms demand labor.
-Financial Markets: Including stock markets, bond markets, and other venues for financial trading.

Understanding these markets helps in analyzing economic activities, pricing strategies, and policy implications.

Label: **Business & Finance**

input:
Does infinite smallness exist? It seems that it should but it also seems that it can’t possibly (See details) For ex:

I think we can all agree that you can’t travel from point A to point B without first traveling half-way from point A to point B.

Say point B is 1 meter away from point A.
In order to travel to point B I must first cross the .5 meter mark.
I must next cross the .25 meter mark, then .125 meters, .0625, etc…

Since I ultimately arrive at a point were I am 0 meters from point B I must have eventually encountered a number that could not longer be halved.

Put another way; The distance between me and point B gets ever smaller as I approach point B.  Imagine a point when I am .00000000001 meters from point B.

If infinite smallness existed than the distance between myself and point B would forever be getting smaller but never reach 0 and I would never get there.  But we know from real life experience that I do eventually arrive at point B.

This raises the question that if infinite smallness doesn’t exist, than what is the smallest number?

input:
Why should I buy a Macintosh? I have to buy a new computer. Friends have been trying to convince me to switch from Dell Windows laptop to a Mac PowerBook, but I'm not so sure. I use a computer for:

1. Access to the web & email. Yep, can do that on a Mac. 

2. Write. Yep, can do that on a Mac. But I use OpenOffice as my office suite; not well-supported on a Mac.  

3. Manage my finances. Eh . . . I guess I can switch from MS Money to Quicken. What a pain, though.  

4. Play games. Oh boy. The Mac really comes up short here. 

It's that last one that hangs me up. Games that I love, like Madden NFL and Grand Theft Auto, just aren't available on the Mac. 

To get around the games requirement, a friend suggested I buy a Mac and an Xbox. But a Mac is already significantly more expensive than a new Windows laptop, so that doesn't seem very financially viable.

Plus, since Apple is switching Macs from PowerPC to Intel chips sometime in 2006, now seems like a bad time to buy a Mac.

The last Night that She lived
It was a Common Night
Except the Dying — this to Us
Made Nature different

We noticed smallest things —
Things overlooked before
By this great light upon our Minds
Italicized — as 'twere.

As We went out and in
Between Her final Room
And Rooms where Those to be alive
Tomorrow were, a Blame

That Others could exist
While She must finish quite
A Jealousy for Her arose
So nearly infinite —

We waited while She passed —
It was a narrow time —
Too jostled were Our Souls to speak
At length the notice came.

She mentioned, and forgot —
Then lightly as a Reed
Bent to the Water, struggled scarce —
Consented, and was dead —

And We — We placed the Hair —
And drew the Head erect —
And then an awful leisure was
Belief to regulate —

input: Why are sports so popular? Please answer with with some sort of analysis, rather than a short reply.
label: Sports
model_output:
Sports are incredibly popular worldwide due to a combination of psychological, social, and cultural factors that contribute to their widespread appeal. Firstly, sports evoke strong emotions—excitement, joy, even despair—which foster deep emotional connections among fans and players. These shared emotional experiences create a sense of community and belonging, as people unite to support their favorite teams or athletes.

Second, sports serve as a form of entertainment and escapism, allowing individuals to temporarily disconnect from daily stresses and immerse themselves in thrilling competitions. The unpredictability of outcomes enhances engagement, as viewers are eager to see unexpected results and highlight moments.

Third, sports promote physical activity, health, and personal achievement, inspiring individuals to pursue athletic excellence and adopt healthier lifestyles. Moreover, sports often embody societal values such as teamwork, perseverance, and fair play, serving as important cultural symbols.

Additionally, sports have significant media coverage and commercial interests, which amplify their visibility and accessibility globally. Major events like the Olympics or the World Cup attract massive audiences, reinforcing the sport's cultural importance.

Overall, the combination of emotional engagement, social connection, entertainment value, cultural significance, and media presence explains why sports hold such a prominent position in many people's lives and why they are so popular worldwide.

Label: Society & Culture

input:
What do you think about this soldiers letter? From:  J.D. Englehart, (Former) SPC. 1st Infantry Division

Sent: January 14, 2006

People often ask me, "If you are so against the war and couldn't stand
the army, why did you ever join in the first place?" I have answered
the same every time, that perhaps I was naïve, that I wanted a chance
to see the world and earn college money. Or that I felt trapped in a
dead-end town and needed a chance to escape, or that I was curious to
live life as a soldier and gain military knowledge. These answers are
never enough for some people, yet so many young Americans end up in
the military the same exact way.

I understand that I joined just prior to September 11, 2001. Indeed, I
was naïve then to think that we lived in a somewhat peaceful world.
Soldiers at that time joined for other reasons. Maybe soldiers who
join now are ones who want to fight in a war. After much personal
debate, I have learned that my resistance to war and empire was forged
by the army itself. Since the very beginning of my four year military
experience, I was simply a very different soldier.

In basic training, instead of attending church service with the rest
of the privates for two hours of relaxation, I was in the barracks
mopping the floors and cleaning toilets. I would not fake a belief in
god for petty rewards.

While other soldiers were marching in rank and file to eat chow, I was
off to the side, being smoked by a drill sergeant--doing pushups and
flutter-kicks--for refusing to yell out cadence like a dopey high
school cheerleader.

As time went by, it never got any easier. I had a very hard time with
the concept of conformity.

While other soldiers in the barracks were watching porno's and hitting
the beer bong with their frat-buddies, I was sitting on my bunk in a
dark corner of a room reading Noam Chomsky.

Instead of spending endless hours spit-shining my boots or ironing my
BDU's, I was playing punk riffs on my guitar or perhaps writing poetry.

I would routinely skip out on company "mandatory fun days" and go back
to my room and sleep. Beetle Bailey was my hero.

Instead of spending every weekend going to the same mundane hip-hop
clubs and discos, starting fights and trying to get laid, I was
backpacking across Europe with other like-minded friends. We traveled
way beyond the limits that a mileage pass would allow. We were openly
learning about other cultures, exploring a great unknown, and living
life to the fullest while we had it.

Instead of hating Iraqis for their strange ways and resentful
behavior, I was trying to imagine the world in which they lived, even
before an unwelcome US occupation forced them to live in a war zone.

While other soldiers were bragging about how many hajis they had waxed
in the last engagement, I was carefully pondering what the longtime
ramifications would be for such inane bloodshed.

Instead of coming back from missions and going straight to the
PlayStation, I was writing what I saw and how I felt on this blog.

It is true that I was a very different breed in the army. However,
there were others like me. We were far and few between, we were
misfits in an olive-drab green hell. We solidified, became friends,
and became brothers. Most of the soldiers in my platoon were this way,
outcasts. We opposed the war, sometimes openly. We were never
persecuted for our beliefs because, although we were angry, we were a
whole. We were a group of covert-subverts and our chain of command
hated it.

I came home from Iraq and was awarded combat spurs, a glorious
achievement for a cavalry scout. I contemplated the true meaning of
these spurs, this icon of war. Spurs that were worn by soldiers on
horses; who rode with General Custer and decimated the American Indian
population. Spurs painted with the blood of five major wars of the
20th century, some wars to fight empire and others to promote it. What
would I do with these spurs

input:
Can y'all tell me any more expressions like y'all ? Can you give me more examples of colloquial second person plural expressions in English? 

My amateur understanding is that at one time, 2nd person plural and 2nd person singular were two different expressions: "you" and "thou", respectively. However, "you" came to be used in the cases of both 2nd person plural AND singular, and thou fell into disuse (not sure when this was). 

However, there seems to be a deep-seated need on the part of English speakers to invent new colloquial second person plural expressions to be able to distinguish between second person plural and second person plural. Over the years, I have noticed that the following 2nd person plural expressions:

you-all or y'all: southern US
youse: New York City 
youse guys: New Jersey 
you guys: Western US
yuz: Baltimore 
yunze: Western PA

and in fact now in Western PA, "yunze" is sometimes used for second person singular as well, so a new colloquial expression, "yunzes" has been invented to replace "yunze" for second person plural.

Does anyone know of any other similar expressions? Any comments?

Riddle logic suggests the answers are: the person in disguise who deals in secrets and lies — "spy"; the last thing to mend, middle of middle, end of end — "d" (the letter "d" appears as the last letter in "mend," the middle letter in "middle," and the end letter in "end"); the sound heard when searching for a hard-to-find word — "hmm." 

Stringing these together: "spy" + "d" + "hmm" — which sounds like "spied him." 

However, the question asks which creature you would be unwilling to kiss. Commonly, this riddle implies "a frog" or "a toad," as fairy tales and folklore suggest. Given the clues and the general nature of such riddles, the answer is often **"a toad"**.

**Answer: toad**

label: Science & Mathematics
model_output:
The question "Do smells weigh anything?" pertains to a scientific inquiry about the physical properties related to smells, which involves physics and chemistry—specifically, the nature of molecules and how they have mass and weight.

This topic falls under the category of "Science & Mathematics."

**Explanation:**  
Smells are caused by molecules that are airborne and detected by our sense of smell. These molecules have mass, and therefore, technically, they do weigh something. The question about whether smells "weigh anything" touches on the scientific principle that molecules possess mass, and in principle, substances with mass do weigh, although the weight is typically negligible and difficult to measure directly in the context of smells. Nonetheless, it is a scientific question concerning physical properties.

**Reference:**  
In physics and chemistry, all matter, including molecules responsible for odors, has mass, and mass contributes to weight under gravity. Therefore, smells (or rather, the molecules that produce them) do indeed weigh something, albeit minuscule.

**Answer:**

Finding the solution to  ln(x)/x = (1/2) ln(2/86400)? Another person here suggested this problem. 

I used the Newton-Raphson method to find the root of the function f(X)=exp(aX)-X, where a=.5*log(2/86400)=-5.336798 approximately. 

This yields the iteration Xn+1=Xn-f(Xn)/f'(Xn) which converges very rapidly to a value of X=0.25560605642100. Starting at X0=0, after 1 iteration, the estimate is in error by about 9.8e-2, after 2 iterations, the estimate is in error by about 1.5e-2, after 3 iterations the estimate is in error by about 3.5e-4, after 4 iterations the estimate is in error by 1.9e-7 and after 5 iterations it has has converged to an estimate that is in error by 5.6e-14.

Is there a better way to do this?

input:
Induction fails! What's wrong with the prisoner's reasoning in the famous paradox (The Unexpected Execution )? There is a prisoner on death row. His captor 
is especially cruel, and so on a Monday morning 
tells the prisoner: 
"You will be executed later this week. 
However I won't tell you what day beforehand. 
When you are dragged out to the firing squad, 
it will be a surprise to you."
The prisoner mulls this over. The week runs from 
Monday to Sunday. If the prisoner makes it to Sunday, 
there are no further days for the execution to 
take place. It must be that day he will be shot 
but it wouldn't be a surprise. Hence the 
execution cannot be on Sunday and must be on 
Tuesday through Saturday. But then if the prisoner 
makes it to Saturday, there are no further days 
for the execution to take place, as Sunday is no 
longer an option. Hence the execution must be on 
that day, but then it wouldn't be a surprise. 
Thus it cannot take place on Saturday. The reasoning 
continues in a similar fashion until every day 
is ruled out. The prisoner concludes that there is 
no way for the conditions of the execution to 
be fulfilled and therefore the execution cannot 
take place. Therefore, it comes as a great shock 
when on the Thursday the prisoner is taken from his 
cell and placed before the firing squad.
label: Science & Mathematics

input: Please explain the concept of playing hard to get.? Everything about this concept is too counterintuitive to make any sense to me. how is it done? Why does it work (or does it), or do girls do it just to blow off guys they don't really want?
label: Family & Relationships
model_output:
The concept of playing hard to get relates to a social strategy often used in dating and romantic contexts. It involves intentionally appearing less available, less interested, or more elusive than one actually is, with the aim of increasing one's perceived value or desirability in the eyes of the other person. This approach can create a sense of challenge or mystery, potentially making the individual seem more attractive.

How it is done:
- Maintaining a level of emotional distance or not immediately responding to messages.
- Being somewhat elusive or unpredictable in interactions.
- Not always reciprocating affection or interest right away.
- Showing confidence and independence, so the other person perceives self-sufficiency.

Why it works (or sometimes doesn't):
- It can increase attraction because people often value what is scarce or difficult to obtain, tapping into psychological principles like scarcity and validation.
- It can signal self-confidence and independence, qualities that are generally appealing.
- However, if overused or applied insincerely, it can backfire, leading to misunderstandings or loss of interest.

Regarding whether girls do it just to blow off guys they don't want:
- Sometimes, individuals may use this tactic genuinely as part of their dating strategy.
- Other times, it may reflect discomfort, indecision, or a desire to gauge the other person's interest.
- Not all girls or individuals engage in playing hard to get; motivations vary widely.

Overall, it's a form of social and romantic signaling that relies on communicating to others that one values themselves and their own interests, which can influence attraction dynamics.

Label: Society & Culture

input: need some help. right answer will be rewarded. show work please? a sample of nitrogen is collected over water at 21.5 degrees celsuis. the vapor pressure of water  at 21.5 degrees celcuisis 2.6 kPa. wut is the partial pressure of the nitrogen if the total pressure in the flask is 99.4 kPa?answer should be 96.8 kPa
label: Science & Mathematics
model_output:
Let's analyze the problem step-by-step:

1. The question involves calculating the partial pressure of nitrogen.
2. Given data:
   - Total pressure in the flask = 99.4 kPa
   - Vapor pressure of water at 21.5°C = 2.6 kPa
3. Since the nitrogen is collected over water, the total pressure is the sum of the partial pressure of nitrogen and the vapor pressure of water:
   
   \( P_{total} = P_{N_2} + P_{H_2O} \)

4. Rearranging to find the partial pressure of nitrogen:

   \( P_{N_2} = P_{total} - P_{H_2O} = 99.4\, \text{kPa} - 2.6\, \text{kPa} = 96.8\, \text{kPa} \)

The calculation matches the provided answer, confirming the understanding.

This problem involves concepts from chemistry about gases and vapor pressures.

Considering the categories, this is related to physical chemistry, which falls under "Science & Mathematics."

input:
Can you give me more examples of colloquial second person plural expressions in English? My amateur understanding is that at one time, 2nd person plural and 2nd person singular were two different expressions: "you" and "thou", respectively. However, "you" came to be used in the cases of both 2nd person plural AND singular, and thou fell into disuse (not sure when this was). 

However, there seems to be a deep-seated need on the part of English speakers to invent new colloquial second person plural expressions to be able to distinguish between second person plural and second person plural. Over the years, I have noticed that the following 2nd person plural expressions:

you-all or y'all: southern US
youse: New York City 
youse guys: New Jersey 
you guys: Western US
yuz: Baltimore 
yunze: Western PA

and in fact now in Western PA, "yunze" is sometimes used for second person singular as well, so a new colloquial expression, "yunzes" has been invented to replace "yunze" for second person plural.

Does anyone know of any other similar expressions? Any comments?

Please tell me that my solution to this question is correct or incorrect, or give me your solution? Question:  suppose U have two bulbs and a 100 floor building. In how many attempts U can find the floor from where the bulbs will start to break. (U have to drop the bulbs from the floor to the ground). 
Solution: Let the number be n (n is the maximum number of attempt, bulbs can be broken in less than n attempts). Start your attempt from n’th floor (1<or= n <100)
n’th floor                                                      -attempt 1.
[n+ (n-1)]’th floor                                        -attempt 2.
 [n+ (n-1) + (n-2)]’th floor                           -attempt 3.
[n+ (n-1) + (n-2) + (n-3)]’th floor                -attempt 4. 
  . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .  ..                                  …………. 
[n+ (n-1) + (n-2) + (n-3) +……. +1]’th floor –attempt n
U have to cover all the 100 floors in n attempts if the bulb does not break at any of the floors you have chosen below the 100’th floor (because if the first bulb got broken at any of the floor U have chosen below the 100’th floor i.e. n’th floor, [n+(n-1)]’th floor [n+(n-1)+(n-2)]’th floor …. , then count the number of attempts and number of floor U are left with,U will find that both are the same. For ex. If the first bulb got broken at n’th floor then it is sure that the required “exact” floor will lei between the floor1 and floor n, as U have taken your first attempt at n’th floor then U are left with only (n-1) attempt to do, but U are left with only (n-1) floor to experiment also, then it is clear that U will find the exact floor in <or = n attempts. similarly for all the other intervals, U will find the exact floor in <or= n attempts ) that means that [n+ (n-1) + (n-2) + (n-3) +………+1] =100 or [{n (n+1)}/2] =100 or n^2 +n =200 or n^2 + n -200 =0 which gives n = 13.651 (n is an integral quantity and 13.651~ 14 thus n = 14).

input: What is maraboutism? A typically Moroccan phenomenon is maraboutism. To the foreign traveller, Moroccan Sufism is most visible in the cult of marabouts -saintly tombs and zawiyas of which (numbering hundreds, if not thousands) are found throughout the kingdom. But in reality a marabout is the living Sufi mystic who builds a Ribat (zawiya with many departments) for the purpose of gathering people around God Almighty and His invocation. Ribat is a verbal noun derived from râbata, yurâbitu, meaning "to station and stay in place". The ribat played an important and major role in the awakening and preparation of Moroccan society since it provided a focus for combating illiteracy and inculcating knowledge, a place of worship, defence of the safety of the homeland and fighting injustice and social corruption. Most of Moroccan marabouts won the respect and veneration of their communities through their uncommon piety and karamat (miracles).

input:
Which number is a wrong solution of the problem, 2 or 4? Or both? Let A=2^(1/2), that is, A is the square root of two.
Calculate A^(A^(A^(A^(A^...)))).
Here "..." implies that the sequence of powers continues infinitely.

Put another way, consider the sequence A(n)
defined by the recurrence:
A(0)=A, A(N+1)=A^[A(N)],
that is, each term is equal to A raised to the power given by the preceding term.
Calculate A(infinity). 

Consider the following solution:
denote the result by X.
Then we have an equation for X:
A^X=X.
For A=2^(1/2), this equation yields X=2 and X=4.
Indeed, 
A^2=2
A^4=4

However, the solution should be unique!

Which number is a wrong solution of the problem, 
2 or 4? Or both?

Can you prove this theory? (decimal period of rational numbers)? Rational numbers as decimal fractions:

Whenever you divide a whole number by a number that is not just a multiple of 2 or 5, you will receive a decimal fraction that never ends.

For certain numbers there clearly is a period: one digit for 3 or 9, two digits for 11, 33 and 99, three digits for e.g. 27 and 31, six digits for 7 or 13, etc.

Characteristic of the number of digits in the period is that there is a number which only consists of the digit 9 which is divisible by the number you divide through.

I'd like to prove that there is a period for all rational numbers whose divisor isn't divisible by 2 or 5. 

Based on this observation, I can rephrase the theory as:

For every whole number not divisible by 2 or 5 there exists a multiple with only the digit 9.


I'm also interested whether this observation is true for other numeric systems, e.g. hexadecimal.

For every whole number in a numeric system based on N not divisible by the prime numbers which N consists of there is a multiple

will you answer my questioN? EXPLAIN HOW YOU DID IT AND SHOW WORK! THANK YOU? a circular flower garden has a radius of 5 meters. it will be expanded so that its radius will be icreased by 2 meters. about how much greater will the expanded area? use 3.14 for pi.

a 12.6M2

b 50.3M2

c 75.4M2

D not here
label: Science & Mathematics
model_output:
The question is about calculating the difference in area of a circular flower garden when its radius increases from 5 meters to 7 meters, using pi as 3.14.

Step-by-step reasoning:
1. Original area with radius 5 meters:
   \(A_1 = \pi r^2 = 3.14 \times 5^2 = 3.14 \times 25 = 78.5\, \text{m}^2\)

2. Expanded area with radius 7 meters:
   \(A_2 = 3.14 \times 7^2 = 3.14 \times 49 = 153.86\, \text{m}^2\)

3. Difference in area:
   \(A_2 - A_1 = 153.86 - 78.5 = 75.36 \, \text{m}^2\)

Approximately 75.4 m², which matches option C.

Therefore, the correct label is:
**Science & Mathematics**

**Answer: 'Science & Mathematics'**

Tips on how to study mathematics,
how to approach problem-solving,
how to study for and take tests,
and when and how to get help.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Math Study Skills 
Problem Solving 
Studying for a Math Test 
Taking a Math Test 
Getting Assistance 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Math Study Skills
Active Study vs. Passive Study
Be actively involved in managing the learning process, the mathematics and your study time: 
Take responsibility for studying, recognizing what you do and don't know, and knowing how to get your Instructor to help you with what you don't know. 
Attend class every day and take complete notes. Instructors formulate test questions based on material and examples covered in class as well as on those in the text. 
Be an active participant in the classroom. Get ahead in the book; try to work some of the problems before they are covered in class. Anticipate what the Instructor's next step will be. 
Ask questions in class! There are usually other students wanting to know the answers to the same questions you have. 
Go to office hours and ask questions. The Instructor will be pleased to see that you are interested, and you will be actively helping yourself. 
Good study habits throughout the semester make it easier to study for tests. 

Studying Math is Different from Studying Other Subjects
Math is learned by doing problems. Do the homework. The problems help you learn the formulas and techniques you do need to know, as well as improve your problem-solving prowess. 
A word of warning: Each class builds on the previous ones, all semester long. You must keep up with the Instructor: attend class, read the text and do homework every day. Falling a day behind puts you at a disadvantage. Falling a week behind puts you in deep trouble. 
A word of encouragement: Each class builds on the previous ones, all semester long. You're always reviewing previous material as you do new material. Many of the ideas hang together. Identifying and learning the key concepts means you don't have to memorize as much. 

College Math is Different from High School Math
A College math class meets less often and covers material at about twice the pace that a High School course does. You are expected to absorb new material much more quickly. Tests are probably spaced farther apart and so cover more material than before. The Instructor may not even check your homework. 
Take responsibility for keeping up with the homework. Make sure you find out how to do it. 
You probably need to spend more time studying per week - you do more of the learning outside of class than in High School. 
Tests may seem harder just because they cover more material. 

Study Time
You may know a rule of thumb about math (and other) classes: at least 2 hours of study time per class hour. But this may not be enough! 
Take as much time as you need to do all the homework and to get complete understanding of the material. 
Form a study group. Meet once or twice a week (also use the phone). Go over problems you've had trouble with. Either someone else in the group will help you, or you will discover you're all stuck on the same problems. Then it's time to get help from your Instructor. 
The more challenging the material, the more time you should spend on it. 

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Problem Solving
Problem Solving (Homework and Tests)
The higher the math class, the more types of problems: in earlier classes, problems often required just one step to find a solution. Increasingly, you will tackle problems which require several steps to solve them. Break these problems down into smaller pieces and solve each piece - divide and conquer!

Superstition and folklore about Friday the 13th have origins that are not precisely documented but are generally believed to have developed over centuries. The superstition is thought to stem from a combination of factors, including the association of Friday with bad luck in Western superstition and the number 13 being considered unlucky. Some historical references suggest that fear of the number 13 dates back to early Christianity and earlier cultures, while the specific fear of Friday the 13th became more prominent in Western culture during the late Middle Ages and Renaissance period, particularly with the publication of books and stories linking the date with misfortune.

input: Can specific performance be ordered on a BUYER in a real estate transaction? Specific performance is often ordered on a seller who refuses to sell his/her property when under contract.\n\nHowever, what if the buyer under contract refuses to PURCHASE the property, and there are no terms in the contract that allow him to do so, even if he/she can't find financing? Can the buyer be sued for, and will a court order, specific performance?
label: Business & Finance
model_output:
Real estate law addresses specific performance as a remedy, usually favoring the enforcement of the contract against sellers. When a buyer refuses to purchase a property under contract without contractual provisions allowing withdrawal, the seller can seek specific performance to compel the buyer to proceed with the purchase.

The key considerations are:

1. Enforceability: Contracts for the sale of real estate are generally enforceable through specific performance because monetary damages may be inadequate.
2. Equitable Relief: Courts may grant specific performance if the contract is clear, complete, and the buyer refuses without valid legal grounds.
3. Buyer’s Defenses & Limitations: The buyer’s inability to secure financing could potentially be a valid defense or reason to rescind, but if not provided for in the contract, the seller can still pursue enforcement.

Therefore, yes, a buyer can be sued for specific performance, and a court can order the buyer to complete the purchase, assuming the contract is valid and enforceable.

input:
Is BigBang Theory proves the creation of universe with intelligent being and rejects the materialism thought? The Big Bang Theory is the dominant scientific theory about the origin of the universe. According to the big bang, the universe was created sometime between 10 billion and 20 billion years ago from a cosmic explosion that hurled matter and in all directions.
In 1927,Georges Lemaître was the first to propose that the universe began with the explosion of a primeval atom. Years later, Edwin Hubble found experimental evidence to help justify Lemaître's theory. He found that distant galaxies in every direction are going away from us with speeds proportional to their distance.
The theory also predicts the existence of cosmic background radiation (the glow left over from the explosion itself). The Big Bang Theory received its strongest confirmation when this radiation was discovered in 1964 by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson, who later won the Nobel Prize for this discovery. 
For further info: http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Bang

Desiding to continue education is a big step in everybody's life. It is an enormous change - you know you have to be careful because chosing a university is like chosing your future home for the next four years. As far as i know, everyone wants to have cozy home with trustworthy family, that can induldge to provide the necessary opportunities. I considered a lot of universities and i dare to say AUBG is the most appropriate and the best "home". I have observed AUBG in the last few years and now I'm sure it provides everything what young people need to prove theirselves. When i came on the open-house week before three years, i was impressed by the traditions AUBG has managed to save through all this time. Since then, I am sure every other college or university should reflects the opportunities AUBG gives. I have always dreamed to study in the AUBG. I am sure that it's experienced teachers and modern material base would help me develop my skills in the mass comunications field. Of course, you can't chose university only because it has the nessecary material base or good hostel - chosing the best university is connected with hard work and realized efforts. Nowdays, the televison is the best  informing media, has became a manipulator all over the world. I really want to study journalism, because i want to reflect? people's voice, to show we should be tolerant to each other. There are things we should change for sure - we need to rebuild those parts of society which slacken our pace. I have been working in our local television as a newscaster. This job helped me realize i am a part of the society and i should take an active role(part?) in social life. I have interviewed many people from different parts of our municipality and i understood that there are still a lot of political, economic and social problems because of the wrong information shown by the media. I think there are still people who are afraid to show their critical  attitude to the economic affairs and the ups and downs of the international market. I really want to be part of the worldly class of people who work hard to provide everyday knowledge and facts. I also undrestood that i can't build career only on knowledge - career means knowledge acompained by aggregate of clear aims and actions which will lead to my profecional realzation. A successful career for me doesn't mean just an idea for the "perfect life" - it is a process, connected with the accumulation of your intelectual baggage. Finding the best university that saticfies our criterias lay the stronghold of our future career and life. I chose to study journalism in AUBG because i know that this is the profession which would never leave me indifferent to the society that surrounds me and because as every young person I hope and expect, that my future education in AUBG will help me develop parallel to the responsibilities i undertake.

input: Do you believe in the future we will be able to travel in the past or into the future? Using a light year as a distance measurement has another advantage -- it helps you determine age. Let's say that a star is 1 million light years away. The light from that star has traveled at the speed of light to reach us. Therefore, it has taken the star's light 1 million years to get here, and the light we are seeing was created 1 million years ago. So the star we are seeing is really how the star looked a million years ago, not how it looks today. In the same way, our sun is 8 or so light minutes away. If the sun were to suddenly explode right now, we wouldn't know about it for eight minutes because that is how long it would take for the light of the explosion to get here.

i already found driver for D-link DI624+ wireless router.but i can not make it work.help me thanks!? Step 1 Download the firmware at http://www.dlink.com.au/tech/ and save the file to your computer. Do NOT run or try to open the .bin or .tfp file. It will not work. You will load the file through the router interface.

Step 2 Open your browser, enter the IP address of your router (192.168.0.1) and click OK. 

Step 3 Enter your username (admin) and leave the password field blank, which is the default password. Click OK to enter the web configuration for the device. 

Step 4 Click on the Tools tab and then the Firmware button on the left side. Click on the Browse button and browse to the .bin file you downloaded in Step 1. Highlight the file by clicking on it once and click Open. Click Apply. It will take a few seconds for the upgrade to complete. Click on the Continue button. 

Step 5 After the router reboots, close your web browser and reopen it. Enter 192.168.0.1 to reconnect with the web configuration. Enter username admin and again leave the password blank. Click OK.
